 San Diegans make history on ‘The Amazing Race’ 
 by 
 Tessa Balc • Times of San Diego 
 Nov. 18, 2026, 6:55 a.m. Nov. 18, 2026, 7:01 a.m. 
 Today’s newsletter is presented by Oceana Coastal Kitchen at The Catamaran Hotel & Spa . 
 Good morning, San Diego ☀️
 Here’s what we have for you today:
 A Chicago tribute band from Russia, a new wave pioneer and alt country legends are all playing around town this week .
 City Council approved updates to Mission Bay’s boat storage program , including a new lottery system for boat storage permits.
 Tessa Balc 
 Audience engagement producer
 Top story
 No mother-daughter duo had ever won a leg of ‘The Amazing Race.’ Then a local Marine captain and her mom made history 
 Sure, streaming has made it harder to wait patiently between weeks before a new episode drops. In the not-so-distant past, we had no alternative.
The Amazing Race remains one of those shows that many anxiously await each week. 
On the new episode set to air tonight, there’s a team from San Diego aiming for first prize. They’ve done pretty well for themselves thus far — and by pretty well, I mean they’ve made history on the show. 
Riley Tejcek and Ann‑Marie Tejcek became the first mother-daughter team to win a leg of the show’s titular competition in an episode that aired Oct. 7. Now they’re looking to win it all.
Riley has an impressive resume: she was a Team USA bobsled pilot and a former Division I softball player at George Washington University; she also won the Ms. Military pageant in 2024 and on top of all of that is an award-winning children’s book author. But she told Times of San Diego that her role as an active-duty U.S. Marine Corps captain is what is keeping her calm under the pressure .
Growing up she watched the show, and had joked about going on it one day. When her mother visited her in Dubai while she was deployed in 2024, Riley told her she wanted to go on the “Amazing Race” when she came home. They made it a reality.
The journey has brought them closer together. 
“I learned that we get along pretty well as grown women,” Ann‑Marie said. “My daughter teaches me a lot as a grown woman, and I respect the heck out of her. So I’ve just learned that we can be friends, as well as mom and daughter, and that’s pretty special when you hit that point of time in a relationship.”
Follow the rest of their race on CBS and — for those of you who have sworn off cable — Paramount+.

 📝 Group files rebuttal of recall effort against Mayor Todd Gloria : The group, led by Keith Jones, the owner of ACE Parking, and Brigette Browning, the President of the San Diego and Imperial Counties Labor Council, highlighted in their statement highlighted the financial costs a recall would rack up.
 🌊 San Diego approves massive restoration of Mission Bay : A long-awaited plan to create more than 140 acres of new wetlands along Mission Bay, and transforming the current site of Campland By the Bay, now heads to the California Coastal Commission for final approval.
 What else we’re reading 
 🗳️ Kenneth Zuniga has become the first democratic socialist to capture a mayoral seat in San Diego County, following his victory in Vista. He’ll also be the city’s youngest mayor at 28 years old, and first LGBTQ+ mayor. ( KPBS )
 💻 Qualcomm filed state notices this week covering 442 permanent layoffs in San Diego, where the company employs roughly 12,000 in it’s most recent 2023 estimate. ( Union-Tribune )
